analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 17, 2026)
key_insights: Oil is lower on an oversupply narrative and positioning unwind, not on any visible improvement in geopolitics.

4-week equity ETF inflows are at multi-year highs while levered Semis ETFs see outflows. JPM's prime book shows net selling of AI infrastructure week over week, driven more by new shorts than long sales.

More than 30% of SPX constituents have a negative 3m rolling beta to the index, down from close to 40% in Q3. The drop reflects Tech crowding easing from record highs. It is still an extreme outlier, which makes thematic trading harder and puts more weight on choosing the right hedging basket.

JPM estimates the market is pricing negative Semis EPS growth after 2027 (roughly -10% to -20%) and flat AI capex from 2028, with YoY capex growth peaking in 2027. The 'Capex Peak' narrative now looks largely priced in.

Technicals (positioning, sentiment, drawdowns) argue for a near-term AI bounce. If the sell side starts cutting capex forecasts, as a widely followed Substack did the day before, negative revisions could follow next year. Depending on macro, rallies may bring more rotation into non-AI.

JPM HK TIG Conference opening survey: AI capex is the biggest swing factor for 2027 (50%), ahead of geopolitics (30%) and rates (17%). Preferred AI exposure is software/applications (34%) and hyperscalers/cloud (25%), versus 14% for semiconductors.

China AI: the US remote-access rule requires a license for any facility supplying more than 12mn aggregate TPP to a China-headquartered company, and covers running models, not only training. JPM expects China AI stocks to weigh near term, would buy weakness in Alibaba, Tencent and Z.AI, and expects MiniMax to underperform. Chinese cloud providers with existing capacity should see higher utilization and pricing from returning overseas demand.

India equity strategy: 2QFY27 revenue and PAT for MSCI India companies both grew 26% YoY, with stronger breadth and fewer misses. Demand held up despite a Middle East-driven rise in crude, freight and input costs, INR at 95-96/US$ and an RBI rate hike. Managements flag further cost escalation into 2H, making margins rather than demand the swing factor.

China macro: IP slowed to 4.8% oya, FAI fell 8.1% oya ytd, and retail sales rose 0.4% oya. Weak borrowing and local execution constrain transmission, and JPM says risks to its growth baseline tilt down. APEC summit relief could protect trade, but tariff and tech barriers remain.

JPM is tactically bullish on Global Equities. Broadening and international (ex-US) have led over the past month, helped by ex-AI rotation and US midterm implications. EU outperformance is supported by about 13% median YoY Q3 EPS growth (same as the US) and positioning.

The tactical Tech bounce, led by US/APAC Semis and AI thematics, is supported by an extreme selloff (6 consecutive weeks of HF selling US Semis, QQQ short interest, bearish retail sentiment), valuations implying imminent EPS cuts and no classic cycle-peak signals such as inventory builds. JPM calls the bounce technical and short-term, less V-shaped than in H1.

Positioning weekly wrap: HF net flows in US Semis were below -3z for a second week, and HF selling extended to a sixth straight week, the longest streak on record. Global HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025, and the global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x.

Global Semis exposure is still around the 80th percentile since 2018, so positioning is not especially low long term. HF positioning z-score is below the relative-returns z-score, so history suggests the rebound may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.

Europe positioning rebounded: European flows are up +1.5z relative to US flows over 1-3 months, bringing relative EU vs US positioning back to neutral. Japan was broadly sold (HF flows -1.4z WoW, -2.3z MoM, all 11 sectors sold over the month), with combined positioning at the 24th percentile since 2015.

A near-term technical bounce is likely after record HF selling, but the bounce is short-term and the market is pricing negative EPS growth after 2027.

Rebound in Semis may not be robust unless HFs turn more bullish.
India margins face further cost escalation in 2H as inflation broadens and price pass-through lags.
China growth risks tilt down on weak borrowing, local execution constraints and tariff and tech barriers.
Geopolitical resolution does not appear in the cards near term.
vol_and_positioning: Global HF net exposure is down 67% from its year-to-date high, the lowest since September 2025. The global long/short ratio fell from 4.4x to 2.1x.
HF net flows in US Semis were below -3z for a second week, and HF selling extended to a sixth consecutive week, the longest streak on record.
The US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 20th percentile since 2015. HF gross leverage fell 4% WoW and net leverage was broadly unchanged.
HF performance gained about 1.5% over five days and is roughly flat MTD globally (-0.3% for All Strategies). Europe is up 1.7% MTD and Asia down 2%.
Japan combined positioning (HFs, CTAs, margin balances) is at the 24th percentile since 2015, with a roughly -2z 4-week change.

Semis combined 6m positioning and price z-score is near -3z. JPM sees a possible bounce like the one after the late-July Momentum reduction, but global Semis exposure is still near the 80th percentile since 2018.
About 30% of SPX stocks have a negative 3m rolling beta to the index, versus close to 40% in Q3.
geopolitical: US remote-access rule requires a license for facilities supplying more than 12mn aggregate TPP to China-headquartered companies, covering inference as well as training.
Middle East conflict lifted crude, freight and input costs in India.
EU foreign ministers meet in Brussels on RU/UA and ME on 16/11.
Trump, Xi and Putin are listed to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit on 19/11.
JPM does not see geopolitical resolution in the cards near term, though it cites US midterm implications for a flatter geopolitical curve in 2027.
EU-UK summit in Brussels on 20/11, and EU defense ministers meet on 17/11.
